pageCache.text:
Alton School
Welcome to The Alton School
We are a friendly, inclusive, one-form entry primary school situated adjacent to Richmond Park. We also offer a full time nursery for children aged 3+ and an amazing outdoor play area.
Admissions & School Tours
To find out more about joining our wonderful school in Nursery, Reception or Years 1 to 6, or to come and see us at our open morning or on a small tour, please click here.
Ofsted 'Good' - January 2025
“Pupils enjoy coming to school, which provides a happy and inclusive place that fosters their development and well-being.” and “The school aims for pupils to become ‘excellent learners and to fulfil their potential".
SEND Resource Base
The Woodland Centre is a Resource Base for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) with associated learning difficulties. It has a specialist education and therapy team who are passionate about inclusive education.
UNICEF Rights Respecting School
We are proud to be a UNICEF Rights Respecting School. We teach children about their rights and the responsibilities they have towards each other.

Alton School
ETHOS, VALUES AND AIMS
Our aims are clear and well established.
All children and adults:
All children and adults are safe
The physical, emotional, mental safety of our community comes first.
Where we are not safe or do not feel safe, we cannot learn or work.
All children and adults are excellent learners
We all share a clear, shared language and understanding of what it means to be an excellent learner. We dedicate time to developing excellent learning attitudes and recognise the importance of a positive mindset.
We welcome the challenge and messiness in learning where asking questions and making mistakes is a necessary part of learning process. We encourage the resilience in 'not giving up', the drive to 'want to learn more' and embrace new ways of approaching learning and encourage creativity in our learners.
We use co-operative learning structures to develop collaboration and the confidence to 'learn with others'. We recognise the importance of independent learning and how it develops through listening, practice, organisation and personal commitment to improvement.
All children and adults have excellent social and emotional skills
We strive to be excellent communicators. We want all to:
All children and adults achieve and succeed
Our children’s success and achievement happens when our teachers achieve and succeed.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Alton School, Roehampton, London - SEND Resource Base Admissions
pageCache.text:
Alton School
SEND Resource Base Admissions
The Alton is proud to have a SEND Resource Base provision. We are passionate about inclusive education.
Our Base is called The Woodland Centre.
The Woodland Centre is for children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) with associated learning difficulties.
Read more about The Woodland Centre and how it is organised.
RECENT CONSULTATION ON OUR RESOURCE BASE PROVISION
Wandsworth Local Authority recently reviewed the availability of school places for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). They identified specific groups of children whose needs could not be met through a local school offer, notably those on the autism spectrum with associated learning difficulties.
To support the local authority and meet the needs of more children in our community, the Q1E Trust has re-designated The Alton School's resource base. Our current pupils will not be affected.
More details of our consultation on the recent change.
Applying for a place in our Resource Base
Wandsworth’s Special Educational Needs department manages applications for a place in our Resource Base for Autism.
If you are considering applying for a place in our Resource Base, there are a few things you need to know:
Please contact the Wandsworth Borough Council SEND team at EDSNAS@wandsworth.gov.uk and request a consultation for a place at the school.
Decisions are based on children’s needs and availability of places at the Resource Base.
You can also read our full SEND Information report here.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Alton School, Roehampton, London - Breakfast Club
pageCache.text:
Alton School
Breakfast Club
Our free Breakfast Club runs from 8.15am until the start of the school day, Monday to Friday during term-time. It is open to children from Reception to Year 6 but does not cover children in Nursery.
The children have breakfast and are then able to play outside if the weather is good or take part in board games/activities if they are indoors.
We also have an earlier breakfast club which starts at 7.45am and costs £1.50 per day.
If you would like further details, please contact the School Office on 020 8876 8482 or email admin@thealton.q1e.org.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: The Alton School, Roehampton, London - Home Learning
pageCache.text:
Alton School
Home Learning
The aims of our remote learning provision were to:
- be as close to our school learning as possible
- give a broad balance of subjects, supported and independent work
- be manageable at home
- enable our children to show they are ‘excellent learners’
- support feedback and connection between school and home
We provided the following resources to help our children while at home: Q1E home learning.
There are also useful resources available from Oak National Academy.
Please also read The Alton's statement about home learning in times of school closure.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Alton School, Roehampton, London - HOMEWORK
pageCache.text:
Alton School
HOMEWORK
We encourage parents to get involved with lessons and support their children with their learning.
Homework is set using Google Classroom for children in KS2 (Years 3 to 6) or by Seesaw for children in Nursery, Reception and KS1 (Year 1 and 2).
If you do not have access to these platforms, please let your teacher know so that a paper copy can be provided. The school may also be able to provide you with a laptop.
Children may also have access to a variety of learning materials on the internet. Please ask your teacher for your username and password if you do not know it.
LGFL - Useful resources, games and puzzles.
Mangahigh - Maths games and challenges.
Spag - Spelling and grammar tests and learning.
Bug Club - Stories to read and comprehension.
Collins Big Cat Ebooks - Phonics books

pageCache.pageTitle: The Alton School, Roehampton, London - LUNCHTIME
pageCache.text:
Alton School
LUNCHTIME
School Meals
Eating lunch together is a really important part of the school day. It is a key time to encourage independence and develop social skills, as well as to ensure everyone has a good meal.
School meals are cooked on site. From September 2025, the school catering for all the schools in the Q1E Trust is provided by Lunchtime Co.
Our menu for the autumn term is available to download here.
Our new partnership with Lunchtime Co and ProVeg UK will bring pupils a healthier, more sustainable menu - recognised nationally with a School Plates Silver Award.
At Q1E, we are committed to embedding sustainability into all that we do. Our school catering plays a key role in achieving our sustainability goals.
Our Silver Award-winning menu includes:
· More appealing plant-based dishes
· Tasty and nutritious vegetarian options
· Thoughtful tweaks to reduce environmental impact while maintaining variety and flavour
· While still keeping meat options
All meals continue to meet the School Food Standards and have been designed with pupil health and satisfaction in mind. If you would like to find out more, please download the food and climate information sheet and the details of the menu changes behind our School Plates Silver Award.
Universal Free School Meals
In 2023, the Mayor of London announced that all primary school children in the capital would receive free school meals. It has been confirmed that this funding has been secured until the end of the 2027-2028 academic year. All children in Reception to Year 6 will be offered a school meal for the next two years, free of charge to parents and carers. Children in Reception to Year 2 also receive a free piece of fruit each day.
You can also download our Packed Lunch Policy from our policies page

pageCache.pageTitle: The Alton School, Roehampton, London - PARENT INVOLVEMENT
pageCache.text:
Alton School
PARENT INVOLVEMENT
We welcome and value the views and opinions of parents about the development of our school. We understand the importance of having a strong parent-school relationship to have a positive impact on student’s learning.
- inviting parents to attend assemblies to celebrate children’s achievements.
- holding termly parent’s meetings to discuss students progress.
- holding open lessons each term for parents to come and see how the curriculum is being taught. We encourage parents to get involved with lessons and support their children with their learning.
- writing regular newsletters and sharing information with parents about homework tasks
- asking parents to complete a yearly questionnaire about the schools performance and development.
- inviting parents to become involved in the Friends of the Alton parent and teacher group.
- encouraging parents to put themselves forward for election to the local governing body. Please see the office staff if you would be interested in becoming a school governor
Parents can support us by getting involved in what their child is learning, reading our newsletters to follow what is going on at school, and using the language of Excellent Learners.
If you wish to give us a suggestion about how our school can be improved, you can do this by filling in the Parent suggestion form here, and email it to admin@thealton.wandsworth.sch.uk or handing it to the school office or by putting a note in the suggestion box in the school office.
